synopsis: The booklet recommends transferring collision-mitigation settings through measured physics—not copied thresholds—using speed, latency, braking deceleration, sensor pose and machine envelope; this aims to replace per-model tuning with per-model measurement [f138, f6681, f13909]. It proposes parameterized machine-family models rather than twenty unrelated models, covering dynamics, payload, articulation, sensor installation and environmental effects, with families identified before the 2027 hardware arrives [f7906, f7907, f6124]. This approach addresses a historical three-to-four-year physical-testing and per-model-tuning burden, but whether the product range actually reduces to a few validated families remains an experiment on which the schedule and business case depend [f2030, f6620, f12373]. NIOSH's work used 145 underground haulage machines in five categories to select representative parameter sets, but neither that precedent nor any published ISO rule found establishes how many representative machines validate a manufacturer's family; a published earth-moving benchmark proving model transfer across a machine range was also not found [f6131, f6362, f6132, f6683, f6107]. Partial pooling and transfer optimization are proposed for residual differences, but similarity must be justified, negative transfer is possible, safe multi-task optimization remains research, and no off-road collision-avoidance application of the discussed transfer optimization and meta-learning methods was found [f6682, f646, f7033, f7034, f7035]. Transfer should therefore be checked with envelope-corner validation, bridge tests, a six-week physical anchor campaign after hardware delivery and a substantially different second-machine portability test; extensive bespoke tuning and low reuse should trigger stopping or escalation [f190, f13494, f10946, f10948].
